items.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The ball broke the window.
options.why: The ball does the action, so this is active.

options.text: The window is big.
options.why: This describes the window. No action is done to it.

options.text: The window was broken by the ball.
The children are playing ball.
options.why: The children do the action, so this is active.

hints: In a passive sentence, the subject has the action done to it.
Passive sentences use a form of be with a past participle, such as was broken.
Find the sentence where the window has something done to it.
items.explanation: In The window was broken by the ball, the window receives the action. Was broken is a passive verb.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences into active and passive.

items.text: The rice was cooked by the chef.
The letter was posted on Monday.

hints: Ask who or what is doing the action in each sentence.
In an active sentence, the subject does the action. In a passive one, the subject receives it.
Look for was or were followed by a verb ending in -ed.
items.explanation: In active sentences the subject does the action, as in The chef cooked the rice. In passive sentences the subject receives the action, as in The rice was cooked.

items.prompt: Complete the passive sentence in the past tense. Yesterday, the cake ___ eaten by the children.
hints: A passive verb is made with a form of be and a past participle.
The cake is one thing, and the sentence is about yesterday.
The cake is one thing. Which past form of be goes with one thing: was or were?
items.explanation: Was eaten is the past passive. The cake received the action, and the children did it.

items.prompt: Lightning struck the old tree. Which sentence says this in the passive voice?

options.text: The old tree struck lightning.
options.why: This changes the meaning: now the tree does the striking.

options.text: The old tree was struck by lightning.
Lightning was struck by the old tree.
options.why: This changes who did the action.

options.text: The old tree is striking lightning.
options.why: This is active and changes the meaning.

hints: In the passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
What was struck? Start the new sentence with that.
Then use was with the past participle of strike.
items.explanation: The tree received the action, so it becomes the subject: The old tree was struck by lightning.

items.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the active voice. The poster was designed by Laila. Laila ___ the poster.
hints: In the active voice, the person who does the action comes first.
Laila did the designing.
Use the simple past tense of design.
items.explanation: In the active sentence, Laila does the action: Laila designed the poster.

items.prompt: Read: The water was heated to 50 °C. Why do science reports often use the passive voice like this?

options.text: It puts the focus on what was done, which matters more than who did it.
It makes the sentence funnier.
options.why: Science reports are not meant to be funny.

options.text: It shows that the experiment will happen in the future.
options.why: Was heated is past tense.

options.text: It is the only correct way to write about water.
options.why: Active sentences about water are also correct.

hints: Think about what matters most in an experiment.
In a passive sentence, the person doing the action can be left out.
Ask: does it matter who heated the water?
items.explanation: Science reports focus on the method and results. The passive voice keeps attention on what was done, not on the person who did it.

items.prompt: Which passive sentence is used because we do not know who did the action?

options.text: The school gate was left open last night.
The match was won by our team.
options.why: We know who won: our team.

options.text: The song was sung by Dina.
options.why: We know who sang it: Dina.

options.text: The picture was painted by my aunt.
options.why: We know who painted it.

hints: Look for a passive sentence without by and a person.
If the sentence names who did it, we know the person.
Find the sentence where the doer is a mystery.
items.explanation: Nobody knows who left the gate open, so the passive voice lets the writer leave out the doer.

items.prompt: Match each active sentence to the passive sentence with the same meaning.
pairs: The cat was chased by the dog.
The dog was chased by the cat.
The cat is chasing the dog.
The dog is being chased by the cat.
The dog will chase the cat.
The cat will be chased by the dog.
hints: Read each sentence very carefully. They look alike.
Check who is chasing and who is being chased, then check the tense.
Start with The dog chased the cat. Who received the action?
items.explanation: In the passive, the one being chased becomes the subject, and the tense must stay the same: chased, is chasing and will chase each have their own passive form.

items.prompt: Change the sentence into the passive without saying who did it. Someone has eaten all the biscuits. All the biscuits ___.
hints: The biscuits become the subject of the new sentence.
Keep the same tense as has eaten, and leave out someone.
Biscuits are plural. Which form of have goes with a plural subject?
items.explanation: Has eaten becomes have been eaten in the passive, because biscuits is plural: All the biscuits have been eaten.

items.prompt: Which sentence is not in the passive voice?

options.text: The bridge was being repaired.
options.why: This is passive: was being repaired.

options.text: The winners have been announced.
options.why: This is passive: have been announced.

options.text: The parcel had arrived early.
The plants are watered every day.
options.why: This is passive: are watered.

hints: A passive verb usually has a form of be with a past participle.
Look for is, are, was, were, been or being in each sentence.
Check the sentence with had. Is there a form of be?
items.explanation: The parcel had arrived early is active: the parcel did the arriving. Had arrived is the past perfect, and there is no form of be.

items.prompt: Which sentence is in the active voice?
hints: In an active sentence the subject does the action.
Ask: who or what is doing the catching?
Look for the sentence where the goalkeeper comes first.
items.explanation: In an active sentence the subject does the action. The goalkeeper does the catching.

options.text: The ball was caught by the goalkeeper.
options.why: Here the ball receives the action, so this is passive.

options.text: The goalkeeper caught the ball.
The ball was caught.
options.why: The ball receives the action, so this is passive.

options.text: The ball is caught by the goalkeeper every time.
options.why: The ball receives the action, so this is passive.

items.prompt: Put the cards in order to make a passive sentence.
hints: A passive sentence has a form of be and a past participle.
Was kicked goes in the middle, and the doer comes after by.
Start with The ball.
items.explanation: The ball receives the action. Was kicked is the passive verb and by Leo names the doer.
items.answer: The ball was kicked by Leo.

items.prompt: The bridge ___ built in 1990, and the roads ___ repaired last week.
hints: Ask whether the thing receiving the action is one or more than one.
Bridge is singular. Roads is plural.
Use was with one thing and were with many.
items.explanation: In the passive, be agrees with the subject. The bridge was built and the roads were repaired.

items.prompt: Change the sentence into the passive. Dewi painted the mural. The mural ___ ___ by Dewi.
hints: The mural now receives the action.
The passive uses a form of be plus the past participle.
The action happened in the past, so start with was.
items.explanation: The passive is formed with was plus the past participle: The mural was painted by Dewi.

items.prompt: Put the steps of making a cake in order.
hints: Think about what happens first when you bake.
Decide which step must come before the cake goes in the oven.
Start with the eggs.
items.explanation: Passive sentences are often used for steps in a process. The steps happen in this order.
items: The eggs are cracked into a bowl.
The mixture is poured into a tin.
The cake is baked for forty minutes.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the correct passive form of this one? The farmers harvest the rice every June.
hints: The tense of the passive must match the tense of the active.
Harvest is present tense, so use is or are.
The rice is now the subject of the new sentence.
items.explanation: Keep the same tense. Harvest is present, so the passive is is harvested.

options.text: The rice was harvested by the farmers every June.
options.why: The tense has changed. The original sentence is in the present.

options.text: The rice harvests by the farmers every June.
options.why: The passive needs a form of be before harvested.

options.text: The rice is harvested by the farmers every June.
The farmers are harvested by the rice every June.
options.why: The farmers and the rice have swapped roles, so the meaning has changed.

items.prompt: One verb is wrong. Write the correct form. The trophy was win by our school team.
hints: The passive uses a past participle.
Win is irregular. Say: I win, I won, I have won.
Past participle of win.
items.explanation: The passive needs the past participle. For win it is won.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences by whether the doer is named.
hints: Look for the word by.
The word by is followed by who did the action.
Check The door was locked first.
items.explanation: In a passive sentence you can say who did the action with by, or you can leave it out.

items.text: The song was sung by Ines.
The mural was painted by Bayu.
The goal was scored by Kofi.

items.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive and talks about the future?
hints: You need two things: passive and future.
Future passive uses will be and a past participle.
Look for will be given.
items.explanation: The future passive is will be plus the past participle: will be given out.

options.text: The prizes were given out yesterday.
options.why: This is passive, but it is in the past.

options.text: The teacher will give out the prizes tomorrow.
options.why: This is about the future, but it is active.

options.text: The prizes will give out tomorrow.
options.why: This is not passive. The verb needs be before given.

options.text: The prizes will be given out tomorrow.

items.prompt: Choose all the passive sentences.
hints: In a passive sentence, the subject has the action done to it.
Look for a part of be and a past participle: been chosen, is grown.
Check the sentences that have been, is or will be.
items.explanation: The passive sentences are Tom has been chosen, Rice is grown, and The match will be played.

options.text: Tom has been chosen as captain.
Rice is grown in flooded fields.
The match will be played on Saturday.
The children are painting a mural.
options.why: The children do the action, so this is active.

options.text: A storm destroyed the old shed.
options.why: The storm does the action, so this is active.

options.text: Wulan opened the window.
options.why: Wulan does the action, so this is active.

items.prompt: Which sentence is the passive form of this one? The cleaners have swept the hall.
hints: Look at the exact tense of the verb in the first sentence.
Have swept is present perfect. The passive needs has or have been.
Make the hall the subject, then add has been swept.
items.explanation: Present perfect passive is has or have been plus the past participle: has been swept.

options.text: The hall was swept by the cleaners.
options.why: This changes the tense. Have swept is present perfect, and was swept is simple past.

options.text: The hall has swept by the cleaners.
options.why: The passive needs been before the past participle.

options.text: The hall has been swept by the cleaners.
The hall is being swept by the cleaners.
options.why: This changes the tense to present continuous.

items.prompt: Change to the active voice. The old bridge has been repaired by the workers. The workers ___ ___ the old bridge.
hints: The workers now do the action.
The tense is present perfect, so use have plus a past participle.
The first gap is a short helper word.
items.explanation: Has been repaired by the workers becomes the workers have repaired. The tense stays present perfect.

items.prompt: The temple was restored by teams of skilled workers. Why might the writer choose the passive voice here?
hints: Think about which noun the writer wants the reader to focus on.
The subject of a passive sentence is often the thing the writer wants to focus on.
Which word is at the start of the sentence?
items.explanation: The writer puts the temple first because the temple is the focus. The workers are still named at the end.

options.text: The workers are not known.
options.why: The workers are named in the sentence, as teams of skilled workers.

options.text: The passive is always better than the active.
options.why: Neither voice is always better. It depends on what you want to focus on.

options.text: The sentence is about the future.
options.why: The verb was restored is in the past, not the future.

options.text: The temple is the main topic of the writing.

items.prompt: Change to the passive. Someone must clean the pool today. The pool must ___ ___ today.
hints: After must the verb stays in its base form.
A passive with must needs be and a past participle.
The first gap is the base form of the verb to be.
items.explanation: Modal passive is the modal verb plus be plus the past participle: must be cleaned.

items.prompt: Read: The bread was baked by Hadi. Then it carried to the market. Many loaves were bought. Which sentence has a word missing?
hints: Check that each sentence has a form of be before the past participle.
The bread is the subject of the second sentence.
Which verb stands alone?
items.explanation: It carried should be it was carried. The passive needs a form of be before the past participle.

options.text: Then it carried to the market.
The bread was baked by Hadi.
options.why: This sentence is correct. It has was before baked.

options.text: Many loaves were bought.
options.why: This sentence is correct. It has were before bought.

options.text: All three sentences are correct.
options.why: One sentence is passive but has no form of be.

items.prompt: Which sentence cannot be changed into the passive voice?
hints: A passive sentence needs something to receive the action.
Find the sentence with no object.
Ask: the sun rose what?
items.explanation: Rose has no object, so nothing can receive the action. Only verbs with an object can become passive.

options.text: Dewi opened the window.
options.why: Opened has an object, the window, so it can become The window was opened.

options.text: The sun rose at six.
The boys kicked the ball.
options.why: Kicked has an object, the ball, so it can become The ball was kicked.

options.text: The cat chased the mouse.
options.why: Chased has an object, the mouse, so it can become The mouse was chased.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The dog chased the cat" is in the active voice.

options.text: True
False

hints: Who is doing the chasing?
Find the subject.
The subject does the action.
items.explanation: In an active sentence, the subject does the action. The dog is doing the chasing.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The cake was eaten by Tom" is in the active voice.

options.text: True
False

hints: Does the cake do anything?
Who or what receives the action?
The subject receives the action.
items.explanation: The cake receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The window was broken by the ball" is in the passive voice.

options.text: True
False

hints: Is the window doing the action?
Look for was and by.
The subject receives the action.
items.explanation: The window receives the action. The ball did the breaking.

items.prompt: True or false: The passive voice of "Sara painted the picture" is "The picture painted Sara".

options.text: True
False

hints: Who really did the painting?
The picture must be the one painted.
Use was painted by.
items.explanation: The correct passive sentence is The picture was painted by Sara. The object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

items.prompt: True or false: In a passive sentence, the person doing the action can be left out, as in "The window was broken".

options.text: True
False

hints: Is there a by phrase in the sentence?
Do we know who broke it?
The doer does not have to be named.
items.explanation: A passive sentence can leave out who did the action, which is useful when it is not known.

items.prompt: True or false: In an active sentence, the subject receives the action.

options.text: True
False

hints: Think of The teacher read the story.
Who does the reading?
Active subjects do the action.
items.explanation: In an active sentence the subject does the action. In a passive sentence the subject receives it.

items.prompt: The ball was kicked by Sam. Is this active or passive?

options.text: Passive
Active

hints: Who does the action?
The ball receives the action.
Was kicked by shows passive.
items.explanation: The ball receives the action, so the sentence is passive.
